coverage.assessment: Julius's 'nothing complicated' complacency and 'I'm ready for him' are cut. This weakens the provocation-and-warning chain. The packet, stitches, ink and taunt chain is intact.
The street setting and the cliff-path transition are dropped. Both are minor and inferable. The taxi compression is authorised and clear.
Sir James's two o'clock line loses its narrative attribution cue. The train exchange loses Tommy's interjections and becomes a single speech by Julius.
The 24th, the two o'clock meeting, 'If there is any reason to believe', and Julius's hedged 'At least I suppose she is in a way--must be' all survive. Nothing calls the Manchester girl false.
There is no premature disclosure, and the suspicion of Julius is unaltered. Tommy's assumed calm and his 'too easy' disbelief are thinned, which reduces the ironic setup of the anticlimax.
Julius's slang mostly survives. His 'Gee whiz! You've got it!' at the ink reveal is cut, and the pause before the train conversation and Tommy's comic 'Oh!' beats are lost.
The romance-versus-businesslike contrast and Tommy's 'too damned businesslike' outburst with the cold rebuke survive, as the plan requires. The Vandemeyer warning stays live.
All four dependencies have their local and partner endpoints present in the abridged texts of chapters 020, 022 and 025.

strengths: All six verbatim excerpts survive exactly, including the italicised Vandemeyer warning and the closing printed taunt.
The continuity facts are preserved: Tommy's 'only the 24th', the two o'clock meeting, Julius finding the packet, and Tommy's sympathetic-ink idea.
Tommy's sense of being followed and his belief in 'the omniscience of the enemy' are kept intact, sustaining menace on the path.
The required pairing of Tommy's cold fortnight rebuke with his 'too damned businesslike' outburst is preserved, with the French digression condensed as allowed.
summary: The revision keeps every essential beat, all six verbatim excerpts, the continuity checks (the 24th, the two o'clock meeting, Julius finds the packet, Tommy has the ink idea) and all four dependencies. It adds no premature revelation. Its own extra cuts weaken a few local mechanisms. Sir James's maxim and Julius's gun boast lose the complacent remarks that provoke them. One Sir James line loses its attribution cue. The train scene collapses into a monologue with a misplaced 'But'. The climax loses Julius's exclamation and some of Tommy's ironic interiority. None of these breaks the plot, but several merit small restorations.
